name: Radish (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Radish (Raphanus sativus) [Vegetables] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, DUKE, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 169276 (Radishes, raw; SR Legacy), sugars, amino acids, minerals, vitamins, fatty acids
Agronomy 2025, 15(5):1216 doi:10.3390/agronomy15051216, radish root sugars & oxalic acid (root-specific)
Molecules 2016, 21(2):157 doi:10.3390/molecules21020157, radish metabolite profiling (organic acids, TCA intermediates)
Frontiers in Nutrition 2022 doi:10.3389/fnut.2022.889407, radish taproot organic-acid metabolomics, root pH 5.49-6.04
ResearchGate 8261995, 'Raphanus sativus (Radish): Their Chemistry and Biology' (principal root organic acids)
FooDB FOOD00153 (Radish), starting compound list / osmolytes
provenance.curation_notes: Raw radish root is a dilute, low-acid, sugar-dominated medium: the dominant carbon/energy sources are D-glucose (~1.05 g/100g) and D-fructose (~0.71 g/100g), with only trace sucrose. Organic-acid load is low (root pH ~5.5-6.0) and led by oxalic acid (~20 mg/100g); malic/citric/succinic/fumaric are present at trace levels. Protein and free amino acids are low, led by glutamate and aspartate. USDA free-sugar values were independently corroborated by Agronomy 2025 root-specific HPAEC data.
curation_added: oxalic acid (dominant radish organic acid, quantified)
malic acid, citric acid, succinic acid, fumaric acid, malonic acid (organic acids, present/trace)
individual free sugars glucose/fructose/sucrose with real amounts (root-specific, not just total sugars)
pantothenic acid, vitamin K1, choline (were partly implicit) with amounts

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all divides components by (components + unresolved ingredients). It counts pipeline-derived components as covered, so it is not a measure of how much of the source's own ingredient list was captured. pct_covered_source divides source-stated components by (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components), which is that measure. Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
